newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM says to up fine paper prices in Sept.
newsitem.headline: UPM says to up fine paper prices in Sept.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Wednesday it had decided to raise fine paper prices by about 10 percent during September.
"The hike will be about 10 percent depending on paper grade and market," Pehr-Eric Patt, president of UPM-Kymmene's fine paper division, told Reuters by telephone.
Patt said the hike was based on expectations that the fine paper market would continue to recover this autumn after a slump which began late in 1995.
"This autumn may be quite good. Demand started to pick up significantly late in May," Patt said. But in August demand had been low due to the holiday season in Europe.
Another big Finnish fine paper producer, Enso Oy, said it had been raising prices of uncoated fine paper gradually during summer by about 10 to 15 percent as announced in June.
Prices of coated fine papers will be raised by the start of October, said Jukka Kilpelainen, vice president marketing at Enso Fine Papers.
Demand for fine paper had improved clearly, particularly in central Europe, but the market situation in England and in the U.S. was still difficult.
